Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank.
Suggested line: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank, shouting about hydration.
Why: Introduces Brick by his tic before you meet him; the hook gets a laugh.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN YOUR TURN - TEN REPS OF PAIN!
Suggested line: YOU WANT THE CRANK? TEN REPS! NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING! IT IS GOING GREAT!
Why: Keeps the challenge but lets the zone's exhaustion leak through the hype.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER. SPOT THIS.
Suggested line: SPOTTERS ONLY. I AM SPOTTERS. ...SPOTTER. I AM ONE SPOTTER.
Why: The intro card repeated his first dialogue line word for word; this is the bible's stronger Brick joke.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: HA! The pump is still MINE!
Suggested line: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN!
Why: The gentle giant shows through the corrupted shouting; sets up his freed self.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... well. The tab's on you.
Suggested line: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well. Towel's on your tab.
Why: Real Mountain trail-off, and the tab joke now pays off the very small towel in the box before.

Speaker: Throwers and rippers
Effective line: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months.
Suggested line: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...Don't tell me. I don't care. Did he, though?
Why: Pays off Mountain's "She'll pretend she didn't miss me" and stops repeating his "nobody's been out there in months".

Speaker: Throwers and rippers
Effective line: No tools, just lats. I open doors by taking a very personal interest in the wall."
Suggested line: I don't open doors. I take a very personal interest in a wall until it gives up."
Why: Rita already says "No tools... just lats"; Ripley gets her own tic.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever.
Suggested line: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever. (The D.N.A. once asked for exact start times. We said "morning-ish".)
Why: Seeds the Beefcake-Necrocrat rivalry in one sign line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. Hamsters are on break.
Suggested line: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. The hamsters get breaks.
Why: Same joke, but now it says the Beefcakes don't, which is the zone's problem.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required for the long way.
Suggested line: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required; Coach Benchley sells them.
Why: Cuts the repeated "the long way" and tells the player where to get the card.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only.
Suggested line: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes thirty seconds, by order of the Minister of Efficiency.
Why: Plants Quota before her checkpoint scene, in her own unit of measure.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. Since breakfast, apparently; even his audience is exhausted.
Suggested line: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. He has held the pose since breakfast, because nobody has told him he can stop.
Why: Fixes "at nobody" vs "his audience", and the joke now carries the exhaustion under the hype.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. I'm Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes power the kingdom on mills and hamster wheels, and move folks by throw and by portal.
Suggested line: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its folks moving. Wheels, mills... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.
Why: Same Path facts in his voice instead of a brochure sentence; punchline last.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Fifteen concern biceps; the regime burned the other two, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Suggested line: Fifteen concern biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival; the regime burned those, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Why: Says what the regime burned and why it matters: the festival and the old king, which Mountain then fills in.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. Today, we train the brain-ceps.
Suggested line: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. I have practised the sigh. It is devastating.
Why: Drops a second "brain-ceps" two boxes after the first and ends on a joke in his voice.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a small processing fee for repeat attendance.
Suggested line: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a "processing fee". A D.N.A. phrase, I suspect.
Why: Says plainly that repeats pay less, and adds a rivalry jab in the Professor's footnote voice.

Speaker: Chet Thunderabs
Effective line: Not quite a set, champ. That's fine. Take a breath.
Suggested line: Not quite a set, champ! But WAIT - that wasn't a failure! That was a FREE TRIAL!
Why: Chet "never a quiet sentence": the loss line becomes an infomercial pitch.

Speaker: Gym attendant
Effective line: Gym's open! The weights are not. Regime orders. Enjoy the mirrors.
Suggested line: Gym's open! The weights are not. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, from the Capital. Say what you like, they never lie.
Why: A grudging nod to Primm's genuinely good reforms (standard measures), in an ambient line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You receive an empty cup. The stand has mistaken protein for a serving suggestion.
Suggested line: You receive an empty cup. Flavour: surprise.
Why: Calls back the stand's own sign ("Flavour: surprise.") instead of a joke that does not quite land.

Speaker: Foreman Gus
Effective line: The Swole Station's lights are back on, and the grid's HUMMING. Take your reward before I turn this into a pep talk.
Suggested line: The Swole Station's lights are back on. Grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Take your reward.
Why: Gus is flat and tired; "HUMMING" and a pep-talk threat read like Benchley.

Speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
Effective line: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels - END THE BULKING ORDERS!
Suggested line: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM!
Why: "END THE BULKING ORDERS" was unclear; this keeps the instruction and the coach volume.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Effective line: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work. Heh.
Suggested line: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work, when it comes. It hasn't, lately. Heh.
Why: A quiet hint that Death is stuck, funny only once you know who Hob is.

Speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
Effective line: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says. 'Standing. Wobbly. Like a first rep.'
Suggested line: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'
Why: The old line repeated his mid-fight bark word for word; this gives the payoff its own joke.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming the theme from a boxing movie.
Suggested line: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming a training-montage tune to itself.
Why: "A boxing movie" is a real-world reference that breaks the setting; same joke without it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Every weight the regime ever took. Behind a locker door, and behind a very sad sign.
Suggested line: Every weight the regime ever took, stacked behind one locker door. Each plate still has its owner's name chalked on the back.
Why: Turns a flat line into a small human detail: these weights belong to people and are waiting to go home.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex
Effective line: The rounds are irregular. Listen for them on the stairs.
Suggested line: Their squats are not regular, so neither are the rounds. Listen for the knees on the stairs.
Why: Fixes the clash with "time their rounds by their squats" and gives Flex a calm punchline.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). The space above it remains empty.
Suggested line: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). It has been dusted. Recently.
Why: "Empty... remains empty" said the same thing twice; the dusting shows how sure the regime is.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: No spotter needed on the roof. He is holding that pose for himself.
Suggested line: Wave, and he will wave back. After the pose. The pose may take a while.
Why: Gives the freed Flex sign a joke in his patient, unhurried style.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: (Town. Stairs sold separately. The cardio checkpoint has been repurposed as a snack bar.)
Suggested line: (To town. The cardio checkpoint is a snack bar now. Snacks are mandatory.)
Why: "Stairs sold separately" was unclear; the freed zone now uses the regime's word warmly.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'll be spotting you for the rest of your HP, like it or not.
Suggested line: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
Why: Drops the gamey "rest of your HP"; keeps the warmth.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Effective line: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. The gym is open to everyone now. Come whenever you like.
Suggested line: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now; come whenever you like.
Why: Shows Clench's first step back instead of only stating it, and pays off Gary.
